solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good news for the farmer, happen!

definitions.meaning: read literally, a crop coming up out of the ground is welcome news on a farm
to arise or occur unexpectedly, as a problem might

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to arise unexpectedly, while read as two words it pictures a harvest sprouting.

clue.text: Huge mountain feature needing rope for climbing

parts.note: a col is a pass or dip between mountain peaks

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a lasso is a cowboy's rope

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs a rope to get over a vast rock feature.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'for climbing' reads the rope upwards, so backwards; the surface pictures a mountaineer's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal is a synonym for enormous, from the giant statue at Rhodes.

clue.text: One may be eaten by a consumer munching

definitions.text: One may be eaten by a consumer munching
definitions.note: the whole clue describes the principal dish of a meal

indicators.note: munching chews the letters up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tucking into dinner eats the big dish of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'munching' scrambles I (one) with A CONSUMER to give the answer; the whole clue also serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal dish of a meal is something a diner chomps through, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: After work, cleans out government office

indicators.note: after being worked on, the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Once the job is done, someone tidies up a ministry building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' signals that CLEANS OUT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A consulate is the official office of a foreign government's consul in a city.

clue.text: What may be rare complaint

definitions.meaning: a steak, cooked lightly so it stays red, is the meat served rare
a grievance or grumble, in slang

explanation.definitionFit: Beef is meat that can be served rare, and in slang a beef is a grievance.

clue.text: Not all monks have, necessarily, to be tonsured

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every monk is obliged to have the traditional bald patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaving of a monk's crown, so a tonsured head is one with its hair removed.

clue.text: Gets the show on the road with the inclusion of the French actresses?

indicators.note: including means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.words: Gets the show on the road
parts.note: to get the show on the road is to begin, so starts
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A touring production sets off, bringing some French performers along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the inclusion of' signals the container; the surface's touring show hides the plain verb for beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlets are young actresses hoping to become stars; the question mark admits it is an example.

clue.text: I love diplomacy after end to war — it can restore order

indicators.note: end to means the final letter of the following word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Someone claims their tactful love can bring peace after a war ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from 'end to war' comes first, then I, O and TACT. Reading the Riot Act was the formal warning given to a crowd to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the Riot Act, a formal warning to an unruly crowd, is an idiom for demanding order.

clue.text: Pilot is bad-tempered, short

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: testy means irritable or bad-tempered

explanation.surface: An aviator is described as irritable and curt.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot something is to trial it, as with a pilot scheme, so the verb means try out.

clue.text: Individual's passionate on a particular occasion

parts.note: one is an individual person, so individual's is one's
hot means fiery or passionate

explanation.surface: A person is described as ardent at a certain moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off event happens on a single occasion only, which is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Outlook for good little relative — no being hugged!

indicators.note: hugged means held inside the surrounding letters

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of, so for
sis is the short form of sister, a family member

explanation.surface: A forecast that favours a small sibling, with a refusal wrapped up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being hugged' says the refusal sits inside the other pieces, after the abbreviation for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast, especially a medical one, so it is the outlook for a patient.

clue.text: Paper money I have cast into fire regularly!

indicators.note: cast into means thrown inside the other letters
regularly means every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone throws a banknote on the fire as a matter of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes F and R from FIRE; 'cast into' puts IVE between them. A fiver is British slang for a five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang this is a five-pound banknote, a piece of paper currency.

clue.text: Sauce from troublesome person with nothing to add

parts.note: a pest is an annoying, troublesome person
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dressing is made by an irritating individual adding nothing of note.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil, pine-nut and cheese sauce served with pasta.

clue.text: Gaps girl found in fine material

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is discovered in delicate fabric full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals the container: the girl's name goes inside the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae are blank spaces or missing parts in a text, the plural of lacuna.

clue.text: Happy-clappy quality in church — weird quality?

parts.note: eeriness is the quality of being weird or uncanny

explanation.surface: Is the exuberant worship found in church actually rather strange?
explanation.definitionFit: Happy-clappy describes cheerful, demonstrative worship, so its quality is good humour.

clue.text: Macho fish will be all right

parts.note: hunky means muscular and manly
the dory, or John Dory, is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A muscular fish will turn out fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine or satisfactory, so it means everything is okay.

clue.text: What upsets us — idle merriment (alcohol-related problem)

indicators.note: upsets means knocks the letters out of their order

explanation.surface: Lazy fun is what troubles us, a problem caused by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' rearranges US IDLE MERRIMENT, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium tremens is the shaking and hallucination of alcohol withdrawal.

clue.text: I am set up in manageable residence

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: docile means easily managed

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so read upwards and reversed

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone is installed in a home that is easy to run.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards; 'in' then places that reversed contraction inside the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is the place where a person lives, their home or residence.

clue.text: People who've retired from treading the boards are demanding types

definitions.text: People who've retired from treading the boards
definitions.meaning: read as two words, former stage performers
people who demand or extort payment

explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is someone who exacts, demanding payment; split, ex-actors are retired players.

clue.text: Wed now?

parts.note: Wed is the short form of a weekday, so asking whether it is that day now is asking about the middle of the week

explanation.definitionFit: Wednesday falls in the middle of the working week, so a time on that day is in the week's centre.

clue.text: Ditch is running into drain

indicators.note: running into means going inside the other word

parts.note: to drain a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: A channel is overflowing into a sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running into' signals the container. 'Ditch' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch someone is to abandon them, to refuse to acknowledge them any more.

clue.text: Get to give a sermon, but not quietly

indicators.note: but not means the following letter is removed

parts.note: to preach is to deliver a sermon
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A preacher manages to deliver a sermon without shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to a place is to arrive at it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Defeated king had to admit diminished function

indicators.note: to admit means to let something inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: diminished means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch had to concede that his powers had shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished' drops the last letter; 'to admit' signals the container. Harold II lost to William at Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold II was the English king killed and defeated at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

clue.text: Worry with wimps turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: wets is British slang for feeble, wimpish people

explanation.surface: Concern over cowards appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns WETS backwards. A wet is British slang for a weak person.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to fret, and to stew over something is to worry.

clue.text: Head of catering demands items from the brewery

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: asks means requests or demands

explanation.surface: The catering boss orders goods from the beer-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Casks are barrels that a brewery fills with beer, so they come from there.

clue.text: Understands report of capture

indicators.note: report of means the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to seize is to capture

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the account of an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp it, so sees means understands.

clue.text: Explosive device in list written down the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
noted means recorded in writing

explanation.surface: A bomb's details appear in a register recorded backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns ROTANOTED round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device used to set off an explosive charge.

clue.text: First on the road?

parts.note: not the leader in a race, but the first of a car's settings for moving off

explanation.definitionFit: First gear is the lowest setting of a car's gearbox, used for pulling away.

clue.text: Spendthrift wife alters when broke

indicators.note: broke means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wasteful spouse changes her ways once she has no money left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like 'penniless', fitting a spendthrift, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a wasteful, idle person who squanders money.
